 Recount set to begin Nov. 23 in Senate District 4's 4-vote race
 KAXE | 
 By
 Megan Buffington 
 Published November 20, 2026 at 2:40 PM CST
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Print 
 Lorie Shaull 
 / 
 KAXE An Election Judge hands out "I Voted" stickers on Election Day, Nov. 3, 2026, in Nevis. 
 The State Canvassing Board declared Republican Austin Peterson the winner by 4 votes on Nov. 19, 2026, in the race to represent Moorhead and Detroit Lakes in the state senate, but the race is still subject to a recount.
 MOORHEAD — The recount in state Senate District 4 will begin Monday, Nov. 23.
 The process couldn't begin until the State Canvassing Board certified the initial results. On Thursday, the Board declared Republican Austin Peterson the winner by just four votes over incumbent DFLer Rob Kupec.
 That's close enough to qualify for a publicly funded recount if the losing candidate requests one. Kupec said the day after the election that he would do so.
 "With just four votes separating us, every vote deserves to be counted. We look forward to the recount process and having every vote counted before the final outcome is determined,” he wrote on social media.
 A hand recount for Clay County will begin at 9 a.m. Monday at the county government center in Moorhead. Becker County's starts at 9 a.m. Tuesday at the courthouse in Detroit Lakes.
 Elections 
 Recount likely after 4-vote difference in state Senate District 4 race 
 Stella Mayerhoff, Report for America 
 The 0.01% difference between candidates easily meets the criteria for a publicly funded recount. 
 Listen • 1:33
 Kupec spent a decade as a meteorologist with KVRR before running for office.
 Peterson is a self-employed real estate developer and small business owner currently serving on the Hawley School Board.
 Becker County Auditor-Treasurer Mary Hendrickson said the hope is to finish their recount in one day.

 "But we left Wednesday open just in case there's an issue," she said.
 She said Becker County only has about 9,900 ballots to count in the race, in part because District 4 only covers part of the county. Clay County, which is entirely within the district, has over 20,000 ballots.
 There will be three officials at each table during the recount, with four tables for counting in Clay County and three tables in Becker County. 
 Both candidates can have representatives watch over the process, and the recount is also open to the public.
 Results will be posted on the Minnesota Secretary of State's Office's recount results page .
 The State Canvassing Board will reconvene to review the recount results at 2 p.m. Dec. 8.
 Hendrickson, who will retire at the end of the year, remembers her last recount: when Democrat Al Franken beat incumbent Republican Sen. Norm Coleman in one of the closest elections in the history of the Senate.
 "That was a lot bigger, I think, then this one," Hendrickson recalled. " ... I do believe we finished in one day."
 She noted recount laws have changed in the years since, and "we are hoping to avoid frivolous challenges," so everyone can enjoy Thanksgiving.
